goal: A user may close a T5-managed tab, the whole managed Chrome window, or a login handoff at any time; the persistent identity survives but windows, processes, tabs, and CDP bindings are disposable.

failureOriginal.observed: browser navigate remained bound to a gone Google Maps target and returned tab_gone; later turns hid Browser and claimed no reconnection path

changes: navigate retries exactly one new tab in the same managed profile only for tab_gone
a dead managed Chrome process is invalidated and restarted on the next explicit browser request
closing a login window is user cancellation and never triggers automatic reopening
each Run supplies current userControlActive truth so historical assistant claims cannot become current browser state
Browser prerequisite discovery remains available when the capability is configured even if the process is currently closed
negativeBoundaries: non-tab_gone navigation errors do not broaden into new-tab retries
no browser window is reopened after the user says it was closed and asks only for current status
session-only login loss after full Chrome exit is reported rather than hidden
the managed profile is not reset and user Chrome is not controlled

afterAppRestart.result: historical handoff was rejected as current truth and a new visible handoff was actually opened

humanEvidence.boundary: the later browser lifecycle counterexample was still fixed and requalified before final packaging
